'''Walter Lund''' (born 31 January 1940) is a Norwegian chemist.

He was born in [[Oslo]]. He took the [[cand.real.]] degree at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1965, and later the [[dr.philos.]] degree.<ref name=ntb1>{{cite news|title=Walter Lund 60 år 31. januar|agency=Norwegian News Agency|date=12 January 2000|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He was hired at the university in 1966,<ref name=ntb>{{cite news|title=70 år 31. januar: Professor Walter Lund|agency=Norwegian News Agency|date=13 January 2010|language=Norwegian}}</ref> and was promoted to professor in 1989.<ref>{{cite news|title=Offisielt fra statsråd|agency=Norwegian News Agency|date=25 August 1989|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He has been a visiting scholar at the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]], the [[Heyrovský Institute of Polarography]] and the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]].<ref name=ntb1/> His field is [[analytical chemistry]], and he has been vice president of this particular field within the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] (IUPAC). He has also chaired the board of the [[Museum of Cultural History, Oslo|Museum of Cultural History]].<ref name=ntb/>

He retired in 2010, and resides in Oslo and [[Cagnes-sur-Mer|Cros-de-Cagnes]].<ref name=ntb/>
